### Change Log (since previous tag):
```
6f32dde1 I got Claude Opus 5.5 to implement a hashing routine that hashes data from a GDS file to create a value to replace the timestamp that magic normally uses.  This method depends on the fact that magic does not ascribe any particular meaning to the timestamp; it is just a number to be compared to other timestamps, and the only thing that is checked is inequality.  Therefore the timestamp could be replaced by either a random number or a data-based hash. For GDS files, the data-based hash has been chosed because it uniquely identifies the GDS cell contents.  That lets a process like open-pdks create .mag files from read-only GDS that remain the same as long as the GDS contents don't change, instead of having a timestamp change based on the time the .mag file was created.  Also:  A few other issues around timestamps were fixed, including not marking a read-only file as modified because DRC was run on it, which prevents magic from perpetually marking the file as modified and trying to re-write it.
```

### Change Log (since previous tag):
```
d8c0b924 I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to remove the "gds contacts" option which was only ever partially implemented until it hit a roadblock and was abandoned.  Since it was only ever intended to reduce the size of output files, removing the function has no impact on magic's operation.  It may eventually get reinstated in a different (and correct) form.
5d61851d Claude Opus 5.5 informed me of a "transparent" option in zlib that will pass data directly through the filter unchanged, so the zlib functions can be used to write uncompressed files without the file becoming a gzip format file.  As I had failed to find that option when investigating zlib some years ago, I had split the file writing into two files, one for uncompressed files, and one for compressed files.  Claude Opus has now consolidated those into a single file and removed all the redundancies.  This will reduce the maintenance overhead of dealing with both files and also eliminate code drift between them (one example which had already crept into the files).
5c3f2102 The version was updated for today's commits.
3bf1e4ba Claude Opus 5.5 implemented the missing handling of the GDS "magnification" record for cell instances (it was already separately implemented for text magnification).  Because magic cannot directly represent scaled instances at any scale other than 1.0, instead a new cell is created with the contents scaled to the specified magnification using the existing scalefactors.  This method allows magnification to be handled without losing information. There are some unhandled corner cases, but since magnification of GDS is aready a bad idea and rarely used, corner cases are not expected to come up in practice.  A new property type string was added to maintain the name of the original unscaled cell.  The property description has been added to the "property" command description, and the limitations of scaled instance handling have been noted in the "gds" command description.
```

### commit 8.3.686

See documentation at https://github.com/RTimothyEdwards/magic/blob/56319630/appimage/10/README.md
### Change Log (since previous tag):
```
56319630 After investigating a problem with generating the SEALBOUND layer over an entire chip for ihp-sg13cmos5l, I discovered that the "maxrect external" operator was not behaving as expected for hierarchical processing, causing the layer to get clipped to interaction areas and therefore erased over most of the chip. The solution offered by Claude Opus 5.5 was to treat certain operators like "maxrect external" as non-local, forcing them to be computed over the entire chip instead of inside interaction areas.  As long as "maxrect external" is used carefully in a tech file, this does not appreciably change GDS generation time, and it solves the problem with maxrect (as well as other related issues that happen not to have come up yet).  I tested the new code on the Chipalooza IHP chip.  The run-time is approximately the same, and the result is the same except for the corrected SEALBOUND layer.  So I am signing off on this code change.
d083bef0 Fix to the handling of instance names (CellUse record cu_id) in a number of contexts.  Some routines had assumed an unlimited length to this record, while others had assumed it to be limited to 1024 characters (or less) and proceeded to write into a similar sized fixed string without checking the length.  Claude Opus 5.5 carefully worked through the several routines that process the cu_id record and resolved all the issues with potential string overflow, and I have reviewed the resulting code.  This fix resolves github issue #564 (while leaving unaddressed the issue of why any tool would produce an instance name that is thousands of characters in length).
c5139c42 Additional work (entirely by Claude Opus 5.5, with my review) to generalize the method of the previous commit to include spacing rules as well as surround rules, as spacing rules are also subject to the problem of the difference between measuring a distance from the original edge to a target edge at a corner.  Discovered an error in the original commit which does not except cases where the rule defintion includes the residue layer type as well as the contact type, since the method only applies to the contact type itself.  Further generalization to non-contact types is possible but will not be implemented unless the need arises.
8c02247b Correction to an issue that has been known for a long time but remained unresolved:  There is a quirk of geometry in which corner- to-corner measurement of a "surround" rule for a derived layer edge like a contact can be incorrect when the derived layer is an expansion of the original layer.  If the derived layer is distance "d" larger than the original layer, then a surround rule of distance "s" to the original layer can be implemented as rule distance "s - d" for the derived layer, but this is not quite correct for a corner distance measured at an angle.  The correction flags rules that are measured to a derived layer edge and adjusts corner measurements to compensate.  There may be additional work to resolve similar spacing rule errors or to identify derived layer edges on something other than a contact type, but as those issues have not come up in practice, it is not urgent.  This correction resolves a handful of false-positive DRC errors in both the GF and sky130 standard cell libraries. The fix was made by Claude Opus 5.5 and reviewed by me.
```

### Change Log (since previous tag):
```
4fab5040 Added a hack to prevent a port from being added to the node kill list in "extresist".  This was previously done when a device terminal could not be found and defaults to its original node name, but apparently the port itself can get disconnected from the rest of the net, which needs to be thoroughly investigated. See the issue that was posted in the netgen issue tracker (issue #108) by Simon Dorrer.
18f3c5d4 Corrected a crash condition report in issue #548 where somehow the tech file setup results in a residue mask for a contact that includes the contact type itself.  Therefore in ResMain.c, FindStartTile() ends up calling itself with the same arguments, ensuring an infinite loop.  It is easy enough to reject the recursive call if the residue type equals the original type.  The question of how a contact residue mask ended up with the contact type as part of it is not addressed by this fix, and may not have any other consequences.
c81b9952 Additional changes:  Moved the halving of the sidewall capacitance coefficient from the calculation to the tech file parser (done once instead of done many times), and corrected the included (old) SCMOS tech files to use the new "standard" coefficient values.
51522d68 Multiple changes: (1) Corrections to the R-C extraction code to better handle nodes     which have the recorded position at the corner of a split tile. (2) Corrected "select area label" to prevent accidentally selecting     unexpanded instances in the area.  Also corrects an issue with     not being able to select labels that are attached to "space". (3) Changed the way that magic interprets the "sidewall" coefficient     so that it is entered into the tech file as the actual sidewall     coefficient instead of being half the value to correct for     magic's double counting of edges.  The correction is instead     done when parsing the tech file.  This measure was taken because     the open PDK values generated by "capiche" were not halving the     value, so I either change magic or I change all the tech files.
```

767cde0e Two fixes:  One by Claude Fable 5 which identified the two possible degenerate cases when attempting to find resistors in triangle topologies in ResMerge, which fixes the segfault in github issue diagnostic message.  The other fix is part of github issue #538, which found an error in the check for tied transistor sources and drains.  However, the other part of that issue, having to do with nondeterminism in the "extresist" output, has not yet been addressed.
07d98a33 Fixed a negative tile width calculation in ResMakeRes.c, as pointed out by github user "LegumeEmittingDiode".  I agree with the suggested fix and have implemented it exactly as suggested in github issue #537.
d6438387 Fixed a second emscripten 6.0.2 regression in the WASM build, this one at runtime rather than at compile time.  emscripten 6.0.2 removed wasmBinary (along with a batch of GL/SDL members) from the default INCOMING_MODULE_JS_API list.  The JS loaders in npm/examples pass Module.wasmBinary to embed the .wasm binary, and because the WASM build links with -sASSERTIONS=1, the now-unrecognized member triggers a hard runtime abort: "`Module.wasmBinary` was supplied but `wasmBinary` not included in INCOMING_MODULE_JS_API", failing every example test.  Fixed by explicitly setting -sINCOMING_MODULE_JS_API in toolchains/emscripten/defs.mak to emscripten's full default list plus wasmBinary.  Spelling out the whole default (rather than only the members our own loaders use) keeps external consumers of the npm package working if they supply locateFile, arguments, and similar Module options.
28483435 Fixed the WASM (emscripten) build, which broke starting with emscripten 6.0.2.  The failure is not in magic itself but in the TCL dependency build: emscripten 6.0.2 began shipping a <sys/epoll.h> stub in its sysroot (6.0.1 did not), so TCL's configure now detects epoll on the Linux CI host via AC_CHECK_HEADERS([sys/epoll.h]), defines NOTIFIER_EPOLL, and compiles tclEpollNotfy.c.  That file also requires <sys/queue.h>, which emscripten does not provide, so the build died with "fatal error: 'sys/queue.h' file not found".  Fixed by passing ac_cv_header_sys_epoll_h=no to TCL's configure in toolchains/emscripten/build-tcl-wasm.sh, which forces the select()-based notifier.  That notifier is the correct choice for single-threaded WASM anyway (emscripten's epoll is only a stub), and overriding the autoconf cache variable avoids patching the read-only TCL source tree and keeps the build working across future emscripten versions.
718e02ec Claude Fable 5 implemented capacitance checking at shape corners, after much discussion about the implementation.  Since it is not exactly clear what the field lines do at corners, the implementation depends largely on an unknown and presumably global constant multiplier;  this has provisionally been set to 1 but needs to be determined empirically with a field equation solver.  At least one rational approximation suggests a value of pi/2 instead of 1.  The corner capacitance can be considered a refinement of existing parasitic capacitance extraction, and since it takes a non-trivial additional amount of computation, it is left as an option to "extract" that can be turned on when a more accurate result is preferred at the expense of a longer extraction time.

Also: Previously, whenever a long-running process printed the status, it would not update at the end, leaving output like "52% complete" being the last output, leaving the impression that the process never finished.
